input.quote: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 is the only non-solicitation provision in the Agreement and it is walk-away territory: it binds Customer only (not mutual), covers every Vendor employee rather than personnel directly involved in the Services, runs 24 months past the term, expressly includes hiring and employing (a no-hire), and has no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches ("regardless of how the employee applies"). It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made "no ... no-hire commitment". We therefore take the preferred position and remove the restriction with a single minimal edit to the prohibitory operator and duration; no other paragraph cross-references Section 12.4, so no collateral changes are needed. Fallback (mutual, Services-involved personnel, 12 months, general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire) remains available if Vendor needs a covenant.

proposal.summary: Remove the one-way 24-month non-solicit/no-hire binding Customer
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have removed the restriction in Section 12.4 so that Customer carries no non-solicitation or no-hire obligation, consistent with our playbook and with Section 12.3. If you need something here, we can accept a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months after their involvement ends, carving out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, with no no-hire.

ops.oldText: Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
ops.newText: Customer may solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee.
